questions.prompt: Why choose one path before rebuilding your CV and LinkedIn page?
options: Recruiters only accept candidates with a single skill
A page that points everywhere tells nobody what you do
LinkedIn will not let you list more than one job title
Employers check that you finished every course week
questions.explanation: One clear direction lets an employer or client see at a glance what you do and for whom.

questions.prompt: What is the most useful way to check demand for your path in your own city?
options: Read global reports on which jobs AI will replace
Wait until a recruiter contacts you on LinkedIn
Search real adverts and talk to local businesses
Ask a chatbot which careers pay the most money
questions.explanation: Real adverts show the words employers use; five conversations show what people will actually pay for. Both beat global statistics.

questions.prompt: Which line belongs on your CV?
options: Built an n8n automation that sends a daily delivery plan
Highly skilled in all of the latest AI tools and platforms
Passionate, hardworking and a fast learner with AI
Expert in artificial intelligence and automation
questions.explanation: Every line should pass one test: could someone check it? Specific work with the tool named is proof; adjectives are claims.

questions.prompt: You have little work history in this field. What should go near the top of your CV?
options: A long list of every AI tool you have ever tried
Your school grades and a detailed list of hobbies
A photo and a personal statement about your goals
A Projects section with links to what you built
questions.explanation: Your projects are your experience. Lead with them, each with its link, the tools named, and an honest result.

questions.prompt: What makes a cover note stand out today?
options: It is long and lists every skill in full detail
It could only have been sent to that one company
It uses formal phrases like 'I am writing to express'
It was sent to hundreds of companies the same day
questions.explanation: Generic AI-written notes are everywhere. One written for this company's real problem, leading with your closest project, gets read.

questions.prompt: A company offers you a job but asks you to pay a training fee first. What should you do?
options: Pay it, because training is a good investment
Pay half now and the other half after you start
Walk away, because real employers pay you
Send your bank details so they can refund it
questions.explanation: A real employer never asks you to pay to get a job. Fees before starting, no real interview, or requests for bank details are scam signs.

questions.prompt: Which of these is an offer rather than a service?
options: I build websites and chatbots for all businesses
I do AI automation for companies of any size
I help brands make better content with AI tools
A bakery chatbot, set up in 5 days, for ₦80,000
questions.explanation: An offer has one outcome, a fixed scope, a turnaround and a price. The other three have no edges, so every enquiry becomes a negotiation.

questions.prompt: Why add a small, cheap step below your main offer?
options: Buyers not ready for the main offer can start small
Small offers always make more money than the big ones do
Every business must legally offer a cheap version
It lets you charge less for the main offer later
questions.explanation: A ladder gives people a low-risk first step. Many move up once they trust you.

questions.prompt: Where do most first clients come from?
options: Paid adverts aimed at people who have never heard of you
People who know you, or who have seen your work
Big companies who find you through search engines
Freelance sites where you offer the lowest price
questions.explanation: Tell people you know, and show your work in public with a live link. Proof and trust come before strangers pay.

questions.prompt: Your internet cuts out in the middle of your demo day presentation. What is the best move?
options: Apologise at length and ask to present another day
Keep refreshing the page until the network returns
Play the backup recording of the demo you prepared
Skip the demo and describe what it would have shown
questions.explanation: Prepare a recorded backup and screenshots. A calm switch to the recording is remembered; panic is remembered more.
